summary: Lower a stable class setter to a C# property setter only when JavaScript property-set semantics cannot be affected by own properties, prototype mutation, or descriptor reflection.

target.notes: Emit a C# property setter under the stated closed-world property-layout conditions.

semantics.assignment_result: assigned RHS value, not setter return

caveats: C# assignment expressions and setter return conventions differ from JavaScript; expression-value handling belongs to assignment lowering.

tests.name: setter invocation
tests.input: class C { set x(v){ this.y=v; } } const c=new C(); c.x=4; console.log(c.y);
tests.expected_csharp: public double x { set { this.y = value; } }

tests.name: edge: own field shadows setter
tests.input: class B { set x(v){ console.log('setter'); } } class D extends B { x=1; } const d=new D(); d.x=2;
tests.expected_behavior: does not call the inherited setter because D instances already have an own writable data property x
